(sec-item-objectjointhelicalz)=
# ObjectJointHelicalZ

A helical (screw) joint in 3D: the frame of marker 1 moves on a screw motion about the $z$-axis of marker 0, a rotation by the angle $\varphi$ together with the translation $h\varphi$ along the axis, with the pitch $h$ per radian. The joint coordinate system is the frame of the markers; a rotation of it is given to the markers as their localHT. Each of the five constraints can be switched off by `constrainedAxes`; with the pitch zero it is the revolute joint. For easier definition of the joint, use `mbs.CreateHelicalJoint(...)` for two rigid bodies (or ground).

**Simpler**: [`mbs.CreateHelicalJoint`](#sec-mainsystemextensions-createhelicaljoint) adds this item, with what it needs, in one call.

## Interface

- Python names: `ObjectJointHelicalZ` or `HelicalJointZ`, and `VHelicalJointZ` for its visualization
- Markers it acts on: those providing `Position` and `Orientation`: [](#sec-item-markerbodyrigid), [](#sec-item-markernoderigid), [](#sec-item-markersuperelementrigid), [](#sec-item-markerkinematictreerigid), [](#sec-item-markerbodyuser)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'JointHelicalZ':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | constraints's unique name |
| **markerNumbers** | ArrayMarkerIndex | 2 | [ invalid (-1), invalid (-1) ] | (symbol: $[m0,m1]\tp$) list of markers used in connector |
| **pitch** | Real |  | 0. | (symbol: $h$) the axial translation per radian of rotation (the lead of the thread is $2\pi h$); positive for a right-handed thread, negative for a left-handed one, zero for the revolute joint |
| **constrainedAxes** | ArrayIndex | 5 | [1,1,1,1,1] | (symbol: $\jv=[j_0,\,\ldots,\,j_4]$) flags, which determine which equations are active: the translations along $x$ and $y$ of J0 (0, 1), the coupling of the axial translation and the rotation (2), the rotations about $x$ and $y$ (3, 4); 0=free, 1=constrained |
| **activeConnector** | Bool |  | True | flag, which determines, if the connector is active; used to deactivate (temporarily) a connector or constraint |
| **visualization** | VObjectJointHelicalZ |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VObjectJointHelicalZ`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | True | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown |
| **axisRadius** | float |  | 0.1 | radius of joint axis to draw |
| **axisLength** | float |  | 0.4 | length of joint axis to draw |
| **color** | Float4 | 4 | [-1.,-1.,-1.,-1.] | RGBA connector color; if R==-1, use default color |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all joints](#sec-drawing-objectsjoint); the axis as two cylinders of `axisRadius` and `axisLength`, the thinner one at marker 0; for a pitch other than zero the thread as a helix of the radius `axisRadius` over `axisLength` around the axis at marker 1; with `connectors.showJointAxes` the frames of both markers.

Settings beyond those of all joints: [`connectors.jointAxesLength`](#sec-vsettingsconnectors), [`connectors.jointAxesRadius`](#sec-vsettingsconnectors), [`connectors.showJointAxes`](#sec-vsettingsconnectors), [`general.axesTiling`](#sec-vsettingsgeneral), [`general.cylinderTiling`](#sec-vsettingsgeneral), [`connectors.curveTiling`](#sec-vsettingsconnectors).

## Output variables

Available as `OutputVariableType` in sensors, `Get...Output()` and other functions:

```{tabularcolumns} \Y{0.25}\Y{0.25}\Y{0.5}
```

| output variable | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| Position | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}$ | current global position of position marker $m0$ |
| Velocity | $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m0}$ | current global velocity of position marker $m0$ |
| DisplacementLocal | $\LU{J0}{\Delta\pv}$ | relative displacement in local joint0 coordinates; the $z$ component is the axial position $d_z$ |
| VelocityLocal | $\LU{J0}{\Delta\vv}$ | relative translational velocity in local joint0 coordinates |
| Rotation | $\LU{J0}{\ttheta}= [\theta_0,\theta_1,\tilde\varphi]\tp$ | relative rotation parameters (Tait Bryan Rxyz) for the components 0 and 1, the constraint drift; the $z$ component is the continuous angle $\tilde\varphi$ for $h \neq 0$, which counts the turns, and the angle in $(-\pi, \pi]$ for $h = 0$ |
| AngularVelocityLocal | $\LU{J0}{\Delta\tomega}$ | relative angular velocity in joint J0 coordinates |
| ForceLocal | $\LU{J0}{\fv} = [\lambda_0,\,\lambda_1,\,\lambda_2]\tp$ | the joint force in local $J0$ coordinates; the $z$ component is the axial force |
| TorqueLocal | $\LU{J0}{\mv} = [\lambda_3,\,\lambda_4,\,-h\lambda_2]\tp$ | the joint torques in local $J0$ coordinates; the torque about $z$ is the one the axial force transmits by the thread |
| HomogeneousTransformation | $\LU{0}{\Hm}_{J0}$ | the joint frame $J0$ as homogeneous transformation: its rotation matrix and the position of marker $m0$, as 4x4 matrix $[\LU{0}{\Rot}_{J0}\;\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0};\;\Null\tp\;1]$; the Get...Output functions return it as exu.HT, a sensor stores its 16 values row by row |
| HomogeneousTransformationLocal | $\LU{J0}{\Hm}_{J1} = \LU{0}{\Hm}_{J0}^{-1}\,\LU{0}{\Hm}_{J1}$ | the joint frame $J1$ relative to the joint frame $J0$: the relative rotation matrix $\LU{0}{\Rot}_{J0}\tp\LU{0}{\Rot}_{J1}$ and the relative position $\LU{0}{\Rot}_{J0}\tp(\LU{0}{\pv}_{m1}-\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0})$; for a joint the identity up to its free axes and its drift; returned and stored as HomogeneousTransformation |
| ConstraintEquation | $\cv$ | residual of the constraint equations at position level, the drift (#565) |

(description-objectjointhelicalz)=
## Detailed description

(sec-objectjointhelicalz-definitionofquantities)=
### Definition of quantities

| intermediate variables | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| marker m0 position | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}$ | current global position which is provided by marker m0 |
| joint J0 orientation | $\LU{0,J0}{\Rot} = [\LU{0}{\tv_{x0}},\,\LU{0}{\tv_{y0}},\,\LU{0}{\tv_{z0}}]$ | the rotation matrix of marker m0, its columns the axes of J0 in global coordinates |
| marker m1 position | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m1}$ | accordingly |
| joint J1 orientation | $\LU{0,J1}{\Rot} = [\LU{0}{\tv_{x1}},\,\LU{0}{\tv_{y1}},\,\LU{0}{\tv_{z1}}]$ | the rotation matrix of marker m1 |
| DisplacementLocal | $\LU{J0}{\Delta\pv} = [d_x,\, d_y,\, d_z]\tp = \LU{0,J0}{\Rot}\tp (\LU{0}{\pv}_{m1} - \LU{0}{\pv}_{m0})$ | the position of J1 in J0 |
| angle | $\varphi = \mathrm{atan2}(\LU{0}{\tv_{y0}}\tp \LU{0}{\tv_{x1}},\, \LU{0}{\tv_{x0}}\tp \LU{0}{\tv_{x1}})$ | the rotation of J1 about the axis, in $(-\pi, \pi]$ |
| continuous angle | $\tilde\varphi = \psi + \mathrm{atan2}(\sin(\varphi - \psi),\, \cos(\varphi - \psi))$, $\psi = d_z / h$ | the angle on the turn that the axial position $d_z$ belongs to; $\tilde\varphi = \varphi$ for $h = 0$ |
| algebraic variables | $\zv=[\lambda_0,\,\ldots,\,\lambda_4]\tp$ | vector of algebraic variables (Lagrange multipliers) according to the algebraic equations |

### Connector constraint equations

With $\jv = [j_0,\,\ldots,\,j_4]$ = `constrainedAxes`, the index 3 equations read

$$
\begin{aligned}
j_0 = 1:&\quad d_x = 0 \\
j_1 = 1:&\quad d_y = 0 \\
j_2 = 1:&\quad d_z - h\tilde\varphi = -h\,\mathrm{atan2}(\sin(\varphi - \psi),\, \cos(\varphi - \psi)) = 0 \\
j_3 = 1:&\quad \LU{0}{\tv}_{z0}\tp \LU{0}{\tv}_{y1} = 0 \\
j_4 = 1:&\quad \LU{0}{\tv}_{z0}\tp \LU{0}{\tv}_{x1} = 0
\end{aligned}
$$ (eq-objectjointhelicalz-index3)

and $\lambda_i = 0$ for $j_i = 0$. The coupling is $d_z = 0$ for $h = 0$. It needs no state: the turns are counted by
the axial position, and the angle is taken on the branch nearest to $d_z/h$, which gives the coupling a single root;
it jumps where a Newton iterate is axially $\pi h$ off the thread. $\lambda_2$ is the axial force, which transmits
the torque $-h\lambda_2$ about the axis.

At velocity level (index 2), the equations are the time derivatives of {eq}`eq-objectjointhelicalz-index3`: the rows
of their Jacobian times the velocities and angular velocities of the markers, see [](#sec-constraintjacobian); the
coupling becomes $\dot d_z - h\dot\varphi = 0$.

| `constrainedAxes` | $h \neq 0$ | $h = 0$ |
|---|---|---|
| [1,1,1,1,1] | helical joint | revolute joint |
| [1,1,0,1,1] | cylindrical joint | cylindrical joint |
| [0,0,1,1,1] | screw with the axis free to shift in the plane | planar joint |
| [1,1,1,0,0] | the origin of J1 on the axis, $d_z$ coupled to the projected angle | spherical joint |

With the tilts free ($j_3 = j_4 = 0$) the angle is the one of $\LU{0}{\tv_{x1}}$ projected into the $x$-$y$-plane of J0,
which is undefined if $\LU{0}{\tv_{x1}}$ is parallel to the axis.

if `activeConnector = False`,

$$
\zv = \Null
$$

(miniexample-objectjointhelicalz)=
## Mini example


```python
#a nut on a vertical screw: pitch 0.01 m per radian, the nut falls under gravity and turns
nBody = mbs.AddNode(RigidRxyz())
oBody = mbs.AddObject(RigidBody(mass=1, inertia=[0.01,0.01,0.02,0,0,0],
                                nodeNumber=nBody))

mBody = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerNodeRigid(nodeNumber=nBody))
mGround = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=oGround,
                                        localPosition = [0,0,0]))
oJoint = mbs.AddObject(HelicalJointZ(markerNumbers = [mGround, mBody],
                                     pitch=0.01))

mbs.AddLoad(Force(markerNumber = mBody, loadVector=[0,0,-9.81]))

#assemble and solve system for default parameters
mbs.Assemble()
mbs.SolveDynamic(exu.SimulationSettings())

#check result at default integration time: the continuous angle of the nut
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetObjectOutput(oJoint, exu.OutputVariableType.Rotation)[2]
```
